title: Unbounded derived and K-flat tensor calculus for finite clopen module gluing
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes whose images cover $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites and their fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, put $R_i=R|_{X_i}$, and let $r_i$, $G$, and $e_i$ be restriction, the sectionwise product gluing functor, and zero insertion, respectively, of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Degreewise restriction induces a triangulated equivalence
$$D(R)\simeq\prod_iD(R_i),\qquad K\longmapsto(r_iK)_i,$$
with quasi-inverse $(K_i)_i\longmapsto\bigoplus_i e_iK_i$. The module insertion and restriction identities remain natural identities on these derived categories, and $H^m(r_iK)\cong r_iH^m(K)$; the $r_i$ jointly detect vanishing and isomorphisms.

There are natural tensor comparisons $r_i(F\otimes_R H)\cong r_iF\otimes_{R_i}r_iH$ and $r_iR\cong R_i$, whose maps on pure tensors are $f\otimes h\mapsto r_if\otimes r_ih$. They preserve the associativity, symmetry and unit constraints. The same comparisons hold for the total tensor complexes, including their differentials. A module is flat, meaning its sheaf tensor functor is exact, if and only if all its components are flat; a complex $P$ is K-flat if and only if all $r_iP$ are K-flat. The induced derived equivalence is symmetric monoidal for the K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]:
$$r_i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\cong r_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}r_iL.$$
For every morphism $R\to S$ of commutative ring sheaves on this site, it also identifies derived extension of scalars with the component extensions:
$$r_i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)\cong r_iK\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}S|_{X_i}.$$
These are natural comparisons on derived objects and morphisms, compatible with the canonical comparison for composites of coefficient ring maps. They include finite coefficient reductions and reductions from the completed ring. The assertions include the empty partition and the zero categories.

proof.text: For restriction_exact, use the existing exact restriction theorem of ClopenLocalization with the fixed coefficient universe. Reindex the recorded clopen module-gluing equivalence through Fin n to handle any finite index type.

For finite_clopen_derived_calculus, apply the exact restrictions degreewise and build the inverse complex degreewise from the module equivalence. Cohomology and joint detection identify the quasi-isomorphisms. Localize this equivalence using the product localization and Localization.isEquivalence. The exact-functor API supplies triangulatedness, cohomology comparisons, and joint zero/isomorphism detection.

Insert an object in one coordinate and the zero object in all others, then compose with the inverse derived equivalence. The counit gives the diagonal and off-diagonal identities. The sum of the coordinate projection-inclusion composites is the identity; transport this bicone through the additive inverse equivalence to obtain both displayed bilimits. For an empty scheme, empty-index module gluing makes every module, hence every derived object, zero. An empty partition forces X empty by its covering hypothesis.

Use [lem-pur-clopen-total-tensor-kflat-detection] on this same partition. Its ordinary tensor and unit comparisons have exactly the required pure-tensor normalization and coherence. Its chain comparison gives the signed total-tensor assertion, and its two detection equivalences give flatness and K-flatness componentwise.

The representative normalization there uses exactly the total-tensor comparison of step 2, so it equips this equivalence with the required symmetric monoidal structure for the prescribed K-flat derived tensors. The comparison is natural on all derived morphisms.

Its ordinary and chain comparison give the section formula and the degreewise comparison. Convert its representative equation from cochain localization to the homotopy quotient using the canonical quotientCompQhIso and exact-functor factorization identities. The model-properties theorem supplies computed and extended clauses required by coherence; unit normalization supplies the identity comparisons. Apply clopen_scalar_comparison_coherence, and expand scalarComposite to obtain the displayed composite square. All statements already include empty components and zero coefficient sheaves.
